cognate: Greek εἰμί (ἦν / ἔστι / ἔσται, Homeric ἐόντα / ἐσσόμενα) ~ Avestan ah- (ā̊ŋharə̄ 'were', həṇtī 'are'), all *h₁es-; Avestan bū- (bauuaiṇtī 'will be') ~ Vedic bhū- (bhūtá- 'what has been', bhávya- 'what is to be'), all *bʰuH-. Greek–Avestan share *h₁es- in the past and present slots; Avestan–Vedic share *bʰuH- in the future slot.
drift_or_renewal: Renewal of the copula by *bʰuH- in Indo-Iranian: Avestan uses it only in the future member (Y 33.10 ā̊ŋharə̄ … həṇtī … bauuaiṇtī; Y 45.7 ā̊ŋharəcā buuaṇticā), Vedic in both members (bhūtám … bhávyam, past and future only, no present slot). Greek keeps *h₁es- in all three tense slots (ἦν / ἔσθ’ / ἔσται; Homer and Hesiod τά τ’ ἐόντα τά τ’ ἐσσόμενα πρό τ’ ἐόντα).
shared_syntax: A totality quantifier ('all') plus relative or correlative pronoun clauses, each holding a form of 'be' in a different tense, joined by repeated enclitic 'and' (polysyndeton): Gk πάνθ’ ὅσα τ’ ἦν ὅσα τ’ ἔσθ’ ὅσα τ’ ἔσται; Av. vīspā̊ … yā̊ … ā̊ŋharə̄ yā̊scā həṇtī yā̊scā … bauuaiṇtī; Ved. sárvam yád bhūtám yác ca bhávyam (RV 10.90.2), bhūtáṃ ca bhávyaṃ ca … sárvam (AVŚ 10.8.1). Same enclitic: τε ~ -cā ~ ca (*-kʷe).
context: Congruent cosmological or theological contexts. In Empedocles (B 21, quoted in Arist. Metaph. 3.1000a) the elements are the source of everything that was, is and will be: trees, men and women, beasts, birds, fish, gods. In Avestan, Y 33.10 has all the good lives that were, are and will be; in Y 45.7 and 51.22 the phrase describes those who were living and will be, and those who were and are. In the Veda, Puruṣa is all this, what has been and what is to be (RV 10.90.2), and Skambha or Brahman governs past and future and everything (AVŚ 10.7.45, 10.8.1). The slab's Vedic anchor, AVŚ 6.115, is a lesser, apotropaic use: verse 4 sits in the slab as the context-after line of 6.115.3 and asks that past and future (sin) release me as from a post. It directly follows the waking-or-sleeping merism of 6.115.3, so the hymn stacks two inherited merisms. The match is unlikely to be chance. Saying 'past/present/future' in itself is generic, but here three branches share the specific frame: the totality word, relative clauses, one copula repeated across tenses, and *-kʷe polysyndeton. The Greek-Avestan agreement in *h₁es- for 'were/are' and the Avestan-Vedic agreement in *bʰuH- for 'will be' link up into a single chain.
phrase: *'all that was (*h₁es-), that is (*h₁es-), and that will be (*h₁es- / renewed *bʰuH-)', with *-kʷe polysyndeton: a merism of totality across time

note: Pivots are almost all Aristotle prose (Metaphysics, Meteorologica, Magna moralia), with mostly empty partner sets (Cato, Lucretius, AV, ORV chronicles). One claim: the was/is/will-be totality merism (Empedocles ~ AV bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ, supported by Homer/Hesiod, Y 33.10/45.7/51.22, RV 10.90.2). Considered and rejected: the Vedic waking/sleeping formula (jāgrato yat svapantaḥ, 13 AV + RV 10.164.3) against Aristotle's ἐγρηγορότες / ἐν τῷ ὕπνῳ. The cognates are real (*h₁ger-, *swep-), but the Greek is topical prose with no formulaic frame (B-9505a, B-9d3d4). Also rejected: AV dyauḥ pitā pṛthivī mātā (no Greek phrase partner in the slab); guru bhāra ~ βάρος φέρειν (generic).
